questions.question: Identify the verb in the sentence: "She sings beautifully."
questions.explanation: "Sings" tells the action done by the subject, so it is the verb.

questions.question: Identify the adjective in the sentence: "The tall boy won the race."
questions.explanation: "Tall" describes the noun boy, so it is an adjective.

questions.question: Identify the adverb in the sentence: "He ran quickly."
questions.explanation: "Quickly" tells how he ran, so it is an adverb.

questions.question: Identify the pronoun in the sentence: "Rahul gave her a book."
questions.explanation: "Her" takes the place of a noun (a girl or woman), so it is a pronoun.

questions.question: Identify the preposition in the sentence: "The cat is under the table."
questions.explanation: "Under" shows the relation between the cat and the table, so it is a preposition.

questions.question: Identify the conjunction in the sentence: "I wanted to go, but it rained."
questions.explanation: "But" joins the two clauses, so it is a conjunction.

questions.question: In "The patient was happy", the word "happy" is a/an
questions.explanation: "Happy" describes the noun patient, so it is an adjective.

questions.question: In "Let's go for a run", the word "run" is a
questions.explanation: After the article "a", "run" names an activity, so it is a noun.

questions.question: In "Hurrah! We won the match", the word "Hurrah" is a/an
questions.explanation: "Hurrah" expresses sudden joy, so it is an interjection.

questions.question: The word "honesty" is a/an
questions.explanation: "Honesty" names a quality, which makes it an abstract noun.

questions.question: Which of the following is a collective noun?
questions.explanation: A flock names a group of animals (birds or sheep), so it is a collective noun.

questions.question: In "This is my book", the word "my" is a
questions.explanation: "My" shows ownership and comes before the noun book, so it is a possessive adjective.

questions.question: Which of the following is an uncountable noun?
questions.explanation: Water is a mass noun with no plural form in everyday use; book, chair and pen can be counted.

questions.question: Choose the correct pronoun: "Neither of the boys brought ___ book."
questions.explanation: "Neither" takes a singular pronoun. The boys are male, so "his" is correct.

questions.question: Choose the correct pronoun: "Between you and ___, the plan is risky."
questions.explanation: "Between" is a preposition and needs the object form "me".

questions.question: In "She called me after she reached home", the word "after" is a
questions.explanation: "After" is followed by the clause "she reached home", so it joins two clauses: a conjunction.

questions.question: Which of the following is an adverb?
questions.explanation: Friendly, lovely and lonely are adjectives that end in -ly. "Quickly" is an adverb.

questions.question: In "The poor need help", the word "poor" is used as a
questions.explanation: Here "the poor" means poor people, so the adjective is used as a (plural) noun.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: "She is ___ than her sister."
questions.explanation: Two people are compared, so the comparative form "taller" is needed.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: Me and him went to the market.
Him and me went to the market.
He and I went to the market.
I and he went to the market.
questions.explanation: Both pronouns are subjects, so the subject forms "he" and "I" are used. By convention, "I" is placed last.
